text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 429 rate detected in prod cluster eu-west-1. Top offending org: SummitEdge (org_9a3f). 10m error rate +420% vs baseline. Paging oncall SRE.

maya: got the page, I'm on it. joining now.

kevin: i'm loading the dashboards. is this a traffic storm from one API key?

jin: looking at logs — lots of /v1/generate POSTs from org_9a3f, long prompt batching, high token churn. 95% of tokens tied to 3 client IPs.

maya: thanks. early thought: protective action to prevent cluster-wide degradation — apply org-level throttle to SummitEdge (soft 50rps -> 20rps) and disable streaming for that org.

ops-lead: agreed. notify CS before we throttle. cs-summitedge, can you reach out?

cs-summitedge: pinged account team, they're seeing a marketing email spike. customer says traffic is legit and time-sensitive. can we carve them a temporary capacity instead of fully blocking?

kevin: we don't have spare dedicated GPUs in eu-west-1. easiest fast mitigation is per-org rate limit cut to protect other customers. can follow-on with reserved capacity if CS pushes.

maya: initiating emergency throttle now. Applying org policy via admin API.

maya: ```bash
# admin action: set org rate limit
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/orgs/org_9a3f/rate-limit \
  -d '{"requests_per_sec":20, "burst":50, "reason":"emergency-protect-cluster"}'
```

incident-bot: Action logged: org_rate_limit_update by maya @ 1791002400. Policy delta: rps 50->20.

jin: started to see 429s for SummitEdge drop on cluster, overall 429s trending down. latency stabilized.

cs-summitedge: they reported a sudden drop in throughput on their side. asking for ETA to restore.

maya: short answer: this is protecting platform. we'll assess whether we can allocate transient capacity. For now: keep throttle in place.

eng-runtime: heads-up — to reduce customer impact we can disable a heavy feature (dynamic reranking) just for SummitEdge; that halves token usage per request. low-risk toggle. thoughts?

kevin: good call. do that instead of raising quota. toggles are reversible.

maya: applying feature-flag disable for org_9a3f. ```json
POST /flags/disable
{ "org_id": "org_9a3f", "flag": "dynamic_reranking", "reason": "mitigate-token-explosion" }
```

incident-bot: Feature flag change recorded: dynamic_reranking disabled for org_9a3f by maya.

jin: token volume per request dropped ~48% for their traffic. 429s down to near-zero. cluster load steady.

cs-summitedge: customer asks if we can temporarily increase quota for specific partners (they have a paid campaign). Their legal/comms want guaranteed throughput for next 2 hours.

ops-lead: options: 1) keep throttle + disabled feature (low impact) 2) grant temporary quota bump via admin (riskier) 3) shift traffic to eu-central if cross-region allowed. Any capacity to spare in other regions?

eng-runtime: eu-central has spare headroom but cross-region adds latency and might break pinned model versions. Not ideal.

kevin: if CS wants a temporary bump, do a controlled small increase (20->40 rps) with automatic rollback and additional tracing. we need a change approved and coordinator oncall.

cs-summitedge: SummitEdge agrees to a controlled bump to 35 rps and keep dynamic_reranking off. They accept temporary degraded quality.

maya: preparing emergency change: bump to 35 rps with 30m TTL auto-rollback. Will also tag all requests with dbg header for trace.

maya: ```bash
# emergency partial bump with TTL
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/orgs/org_9a3f/rate-limit \
  -d '{"requests_per_sec":35, "burst":80, "ttl_minutes":30, "notes":"cs approved temporary bump"}'
```

incident-bot: Action logged: org_rate_limit_update by maya @ 1791003120. TTL=30m.

jin: monitoring metrics after bump — slight increase in tokens, cluster P99 still OK, no new 429s for other orgs.

ops-lead: good. add an alert to auto-revoke if cluster error rate rises >20% in next 30m.

eng-runtime: added circuit rule: if cluster 429_rate > 0.2 for 5m, immediately revert org_9a3f to 20rps and re-enable previous protection.

maya: noted. manual handoff incoming — i'm going offline in 8m for scheduled break, handing to kevin. kevin, take over post-bump monitoring.

kevin: taking handoff. I'll watch dashboards and the auto-revoke guard. tagging @sre_pager in case we need escalation.

cs-summitedge: customer thanks team. they've resumed campaign at reduced Qo. will update CS if they push more.

incident-bot: Auto-revoke guard triggered? No. 30m TTL expiry scheduled at 1791004920.

kevin: TTL expired, no alerts fired. rolling baseline back to default limits but keeping dynamic_reranking disabled for another 24h per CS request.

maya: final verification: cluster metrics normal, no lingering errors. marking incident as mitigated.

ops-lead: file a short incident note: cause = marketing-driven spike from SummitEdge; mitigations = org-level throttle, feature-flag disable, temporary quota bump with TTL; follow-up = discuss reserve options + quota guardrails with account team.

cs-summitedge: I'll schedule customer call to propose Dedicated floor for future campaigns.

kevin: closing thread. thanks all :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident closed: incident_id=INC-2026-1791002345. Duration 42m. Severity: S2. Participants: maya, kevin, jin, ops-lead, cs-summitedge, eng-runtime.
